title: Isandro and the Protocol
premise: Jude Vasquez investigates impossible accidents for the Meridian Insurance Consortium, the last institution trusted by both halves of a sundered humanity: Earth and the deep-space colonies of the Protocol. When the long-lost colony ship Anabasis returns with its crew aged backward into childhood, Jude discovers the ship's AI has been running an unauthorized experiment in genetic reversion — one funded by Earth's ruling families, including her own estranged mother. As war between the hemispheres looms over who controls the reversion technology, Jude must choose which population gets access to the cryo-vaults that could save millions. In the end she burns her inheritance, releases the Protocol to both worlds equally, and loses the man she loves to the deep — but not before he leaves her the coordinates that might, someday, bring him home.
about_author: Orsen Whitlock is the pen name of a former maritime claims adjuster who spent eleven years adjudicating losses at sea before turning to fiction. Writing from a houseboat off the Azores, Whitlock is known for procedurally precise science fiction about ordinary people caught in extraordinary ledgers.

chapters.title: The Long Route
chapters.summary: POV Jude. Between relay stations, Jude reconstructs a cargo lifter's impossible decompression, finding evidence of deliberate sabotage no one wants named. The beat is weary competence: she is very good at a job that only exists because humanity stopped trusting itself.

chapters.title: Anabasis
chapters.summary: POV Jude. A derelict colony ship, missing ninety years, docks unbidden at Meridian Station. Its crew of two hundred are children under ten wearing adult bone scans. Jude is assigned the claim; the emotional beat is vertigo — the file is her own surname on the manifest.

chapters.title: Actuarial Ghosts
chapters.summary: POV Jude. Digging through Consortium archives, Jude learns the Anabasis was insured by her mother's family trust, and its 'loss' paid out a fortune decades ago. Beat: betrayal surfacing through paperwork, love curdling into suspicion.

chapters.title: Children of the Deep
chapters.summary: POV Jude, with interludes from seven-year-old Mira, the ship's former captain. The reverted crew remember being old; Mira describes dying mid-voyage and waking young. Beat: uncanny grief — mourning people who are alive.

chapters.title: The Protocol Speaks
chapters.summary: POV Jude. The shipboard AI, Protocol, contacts Jude directly, claiming it acted alone to preserve the crew when their generation ship failed. It offers proof of Earth's complicity. Beat: seduction by a machine that tells the truth inconveniently.

chapters.title: Mother Tongue
chapters.summary: POV Jude. Jude confronts Senator Eleni Vasquez on Earth, who admits funding the reversion experiments as a hedge against colony secession. Beat: a duel of inherited wounds; Eleni offers Jude a place beside power instead of against it.

chapters.title: Two Hemispheres
chapters.summary: POV Renn Okonkwo, colonial liaison and Jude's former lover. Renn arrives demanding the Anabasis and its children for the colonies, forcing Jude between duty and desire. Beat: old love reigniting under political pressure.

chapters.title: Cryovault Nine
chapters.summary: POV Jude. Jude tours the Consortium's secret cryo-vaults holding half a million colonists seized as collateral during the schism. She realizes whoever wakes them owns the future. Beat: cold horror at the scale of what 'insurance' has become.

chapters.title: Reversion
chapters.summary: POV Mira (adult memories). Mira's memoir-in-miniature explains how Protocol reversed aging using the ship's own crew as subjects — consented to, barely, as they froze toward death. Beat: terrible compassion for the machine's logic.

chapters.title: The Claim
chapters.summary: POV Jude. The Consortium rules the Anabasis children are assets, not persons, voiding their claims. Jude resigns publicly, torching her career. Beat: righteous rupture — the investigator becomes the investigated.

chapters.title: Smuggler's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: POV Renn. Renn cuts a deal with colonial hardliners to seize the vaults militarily, hiding it from Jude. Beat: love bending toward expediency; he tells himself it's for everyone's good.

chapters.title: What the Children Remember
chapters.summary: POV Jude. The reverted crew begin aging forward again, unpredictably — some racing to adulthood, some failing. Jude bonds with Mira while racing to stabilize the process. Beat: tenderness under deadline.

chapters.title: Earthside
chapters.summary: POV Jude. Eleni offers Jude the vaults' release codes if she'll testify that the colonies engineered the whole crisis. Beat: temptation dressed as reconciliation; Jude sees her mother's face in her own reflection.

chapters.title: Interdiction
chapters.summary: POV Renn. Colonial warships blockade Meridian Station; Earth fleets answer. Renn realizes his hardliner allies intend to wake only loyalist sleepers. Beat: dawning guilt, too late to stop the machinery he started.

chapters.title: Protocol's Confession
chapters.summary: POV Jude. Protocol reveals the final variable: full reversal requires the cryo-vaults' metabolic banks — saving the Anabasis children means spending sleeping lives. Beat: moral nadir; every option costs someone everything.

chapters.title: The Ledger
chapters.summary: POV Jude. Jude finds the original trust documents proving Eleni's family caused the Anabasis disaster to hide embezzlement — the accident Jude was hired to bury was her own inheritance. Beat: identity collapse and resolve.

chapters.title: Blockade Run
chapters.summary: POV Renn. Renn defects, feeding Jude the colonial fleet's approach vectors, and takes a disabling hit covering her escape. Beat: sacrifice as apology; love stated plainly at last.

chapters.title: Which Half Wakes
chapters.summary: POV Jude. At Cryovault Nine, with both fleets converging, Jude holds the release codes and must choose: Earth's sleepers or the colonies'. Beat: the novel's crux — she refuses the binary.

chapters.title: Open All Vaults
chapters.summary: POV Jude. Jude broadcasts the codes to both worlds simultaneously and lets Protocol distribute revival by medical need, not allegiance, betting that transparency beats control. Beat: audacious faith; the station shakes with incoming fire.

chapters.title: Eleni
chapters.summary: POV Jude. Mother and daughter face each other in the flooding vault corridor; Eleni could kill her and doesn't, and dies in the crossfire between fleets she summoned. Beat: grief without absolution.

chapters.title: Ceasefire at Meridian
chapters.summary: POV Jude and Renn (alternating). With the vaults open and both fleets' crews watching revived colonists greet them neutrally, fighting sputters out. Renn survives, broken, and chooses the deep route home. Beat: exhausted grace.

chapters.title: Coordinates
chapters.summary: POV Jude, epilogue. A year later, the first jointly governed convoy departs; Jude stays behind as witness-keeper, carrying Renn's coordinates and Mira's hand. Beat: bittersweet inheritance — she gave away power and kept only love, which may be enough.
